line.text: Mako is already on your couch, controller in hand, scoreboard on screen: MAKO 3, YOU 2.
Took you long enough. I already warmed up. Your controller's the one with the sticky button.
You warmed up. For paw hockey.
It's called practice. You'd know if you ever won.
She says it without looking away from the screen, ears angled toward you anyway.
First to five. No pausing. No excuses about lag. And you're going down.
You keep saying that like it's going to happen.
The scoreboard updates before she finishes talking. Her tail flick stops mid-motion.
Okay. That's 4-4. Which means nothing. It means the game is working.
It means I'm about to win.
It means you got lucky twice. There's a difference. I'm tracking it.

choice.prompt: The match is one goal from over. She's gripping the controller like it owes her

options.text: You're really not going to let me win, are you?

reaction.text: Let you? I'm not letting you do anything. I'm beating you. Different verb.
Her ears swivel forward, fully focused on the screen and, somehow, on you.

options.text: I could still throw this if you want.

reaction.text: Don't. Seriously. That's not - just play the game.

options.text: Nice of you to keep score. Very generous.

reaction.text: I'm not being nice. I'm being accurate. There's a scoreboard. It's right there.

desc: A rematch at paw hockey on the old console; she keeps score out loud.
